title: 2 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who was responsible for destroying all the royal seed after the death of Ahaziah?
questions.correctAnswer: Athaliah
questions.explanation: Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, destroyed all the seed royal after Ahaziah's death as stated in 2 Kings 11:1.

questions.question: Who hid Joash to protect him from Athaliah?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehosheba
questions.explanation: Jehosheba, daughter of king Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash and hid him from Athaliah as recorded in 2 Kings 11:2.

questions.question: For how many years was Joash hidden in the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Six years
questions.explanation: Joash was hidden in the house of the LORD for six years while Athaliah reigned, according to 2 Kings 11:3.

questions.question: What did Jehoiada do in the seventh year regarding the rulers and captains?
options: He made a covenant and took an oath with them
He sent them away from the temple
questions.correctAnswer: He made a covenant and took an oath with them
questions.explanation: In the seventh year, Jehoiada brought the rulers and captains to the house of the LORD, made a covenant, and took an oath of them as stated in 2 Kings 11:4.

questions.question: According to Jehoiada's command, what fraction of the men entering on the Sabbath were to be keepers of the watch of the king's house?
questions.correctAnswer: A third part
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commanded that a third part of those entering on the Sabbath keep watch of the king's house as found in 2 Kings 11:5.

questions.question: Where were the other two thirds of the watchmen stationed according to Jehoiada's instructions?
options: At the gate of Sur and the gate behind the guard
At the palace entrance and the city gate
On the temple roof and the city walls
At the king's chamber and the altar
questions.correctAnswer: At the gate of Sur and the gate behind the guard
questions.explanation: Jehoiada instructed that one third be at the gate of Sur and another third at the gate behind the guard, as detailed in 2 Kings 11:6.

questions.question: True or False: Two parts of all those who go forth on the Sabbath were assigned to keep watch of the house of the LORD about the king.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 11:7 states that two parts of all who go forth on the Sabbath shall keep the watch of the house of the LORD about the king.

questions.question: What was the command regarding anyone who came within the ranges around the king?
questions.correctAnswer: Let him be slain
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commanded that anyone coming within the ranges around the king should be slain, as instructed in 2 Kings 11:8.

questions.question: True or False: The captains over the hundreds disobeyed Jehoiada's commands regarding the watch on the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:9 states that the captains did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest commanded, showing obedience.

questions.question: What weapons of king David were given to the captains over the hundreds by the priest?
questions.correctAnswer: Spears and shields
questions.explanation: Jehoiada gave the captains king David's spears and shields that were in the temple of the LORD as described in 2 Kings 11:10.

questions.question: True or False: The guard stood with weapons in hand from the right corner of the temple to the left corner, along by the altar and temple.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:11 confirms the guard stood with weapons from the right corner to the left corner of the temple, along by the altar.

questions.question: Who was crowned and anointed king in the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Joash
questions.explanation: Jehoiada brought forth Joash, put the crown upon him, anointed him, and made him king as recorded in 2 Kings 11:12.

questions.question: What did Athaliah cry out when she saw the king standing in the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Treason, Treason
questions.explanation: Upon seeing the king, Athaliah rent her clothes and cried, 'Treason, Treason' as described in 2 Kings 11:14.

questions.question: What order did Jehoiada give concerning Athaliah after she cried out treason?
options: Have her taken outside the ranges and killed
Let her stay in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Have her taken outside the ranges and killed
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commanded the captains to take Athaliah outside the ranges and kill her, but not in the house of the LORD, as seen in 2 Kings 11:15.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 11, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: A third part of the watch shall be at the gate of Sur
Jehoiada took an oath of the rulers and captains
Athaliah destroyed all the seed royal
Jehoiada gave the captains king David's spears and shields
questions.correctAnswer: Athaliah destroyed all the seed royal
questions.explanation: According to the chapter, Athaliah's destruction of the seed royal occurs first in verse 1 before Jehoiada's covenant, watch assignments, and giving of weapons.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 11:8, what was the instruction given about those who come within the ranges where the king is guarded?
options: They were to be welcomed and honored
questions.correctAnswer: They should be slain
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:8 instructs that anyone who comes within the ranges around the king must be slain, emphasizing the protection around the king as he goes out and comes in.

questions.question: How did the captains respond to Jehoiada the priest's commands regarding the watch on the sabbath according to 2 Kings 11:9?
options: They fully obeyed and brought their men to Jehoiada
questions.correctAnswer: They fully obeyed and brought their men to Jehoiada
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that the captains acted according to all Jehoiada's commands and brought their men who were on duty on the sabbath to the priest, showing full obedience.

questions.question: What special items did Jehoiada give to the captains over hundreds as described in 2 Kings 11:10?
questions.correctAnswer: King David's spears and shields
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:10 reveals that Jehoiada gave the captains king David's spears and shields which were kept in the temple, signifying royal authority and protection.

questions.question: Where did the guard stand as they protected the king according to 2 Kings 11:11?
options: From the right corner of the temple to the left corner along by the altar and temple
questions.correctAnswer: From the right corner of the temple to the left corner along by the altar and temple
questions.explanation: Verse 11 describes the guard standing fully armed around the king, covering the temple's right and left corners and by the altar to provide comprehensive protection.

questions.question: What event took place when Jehoiada brought forth the king's son, according to 2 Kings 11:12?
options: The king's son was hidden again
The king's son was crowned, anointed, and made king with the people shouting 'God save the king'
The king's son fled from the temple
The king's son was taken prisoner
questions.correctAnswer: The king's son was crowned, anointed, and made king with the people shouting 'God save the king'
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explains that the king's son was crowned, anointed, and made king, and the people expressed their approval by clapping and shouting 'God save the king'.

questions.question: What did Athaliah do when she heard the noise of the guard and the people in the temple as described in 2 Kings 11:13?
options: She went into the temple to the people
She gathered her troops to fight
questions.correctAnswer: She went into the temple to the people
questions.explanation: According to verse 13, Athaliah responded to the noise by coming into the temple among the people, indicating her awareness and confrontation of the event.

questions.question: What was Athaliah's reaction upon seeing the king standing by a pillar with the princes and trumpeters as described in 2 Kings 11:14?
options: She rent her clothes and cried 'Treason, Treason'
questions.correctAnswer: She rent her clothes and cried 'Treason, Treason'
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes Athaliah's dramatic reaction of tearing her clothes and shouting 'Treason, Treason' upon seeing the king and the rejoicing people.

questions.question: What command did Jehoiada give regarding Athaliah and those who followed her according to 2 Kings 11:15?
options: To kill Athaliah in the house of the LORD
To take Athaliah out without the ranges and kill any who followed her
questions.correctAnswer: To take Athaliah out without the ranges and kill any who followed her
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states that Jehoiada commanded the captains to bring Athaliah out without the guarded area and kill anyone following her, but not to kill her inside the house of the LORD.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 11:16 describe the place where Athaliah was slain?
options: Inside the temple of the LORD
By the way where horses come into the king's house
questions.correctAnswer: By the way where horses come into the king's house
questions.explanation: Verse 16 specifies that Athaliah was slain on the path by which horses entered the king's house, outside the temple, respecting the sanctity of the LORD's house.

questions.question: What covenant did Jehoiada make as recorded in 2 Kings 11:17?
options: Between the king and the priests only
Between the LORD and the king and the people, ensuring they would be the LORD's people
Between the king and foreign nations
Between the people and the temple guards
questions.correctAnswer: Between the LORD and the king and the people, ensuring they would be the LORD's people
questions.explanation: Verse 17 explains that Jehoiada established a covenant linking the LORD, the king, and the people so that the people would belong to the LORD and also be united with the king.

questions.question: After Athaliah was removed, what did the people do to the house of Baal as described in 2 Kings 11:18?
options: They broke down the altars and images and killed the priest of Baal
They converted it into a temple for the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They broke down the altars and images and killed the priest of Baal
questions.explanation: Verse 18 records that the people destroyed the house of Baal by breaking its altars and images and killing Mattan the priest, showing a return to proper worship.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction after Jehoash was seated on the throne according to 2 Kings 11:20?
options: They rejoiced and the city was quiet
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced and the city was quiet
questions.explanation: Verse 20 describes the people's joy and the peacefulness of the city following Jehoash's ascension, which reflects stability and approval.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 11:21, Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 21 clearly states that Jehoash was seven years old when he began his reign, indicating a young king ascending the throne.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 11:12-14, the people were silent and fearful when the king was revealed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 show that the people rejoiced and blew trumpets when the king was revealed, indicating celebration rather than silence or fear.

questions.question: True or False: Based on 2 Kings 11:8-9, the instructions to keep watch and be armed around the king demonstrates the importance of protecting God's appointed leaders.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 show that the king was carefully guarded with weapons and watchmen, emphasizing the biblical principle of honoring and safeguarding God's chosen rulers.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 11:15, why did Jehoiada command that Athaliah not be slain in the house of the LORD?
options: Because the temple was considered holy and should not be defiled with blood
Because Athaliah was under a special divine protection
Because Jehoiada wanted to publicly humiliate her first
Because the king forbade violence in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because the temple was considered holy and should not be defiled with blood
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:15 states that Jehoiada had said, 'Let her not be slain in the house of the LORD,' indicating the sanctity of the temple forbade murder within it. This respects the holiness of the LORD's house.

questions.question: Where was Athaliah killed according to 2 Kings 11:16?
options: Beside the king's house by the horse entryway
Inside the temple of the LORD
At the gate of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: Beside the king's house by the horse entryway
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:16 describes that Athaliah was taken by the way where the horses came into the king's house and there she was slain, outside the temple as per Jehoiada's command.

questions.question: What covenant did Jehoiada make according to 2 Kings 11:17?
options: A covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people to be the LORD's people
A covenant between the king and the surrounding nations for peace
A covenant between the priests to keep the temple holy
A covenant between the guards to protect the king
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people to be the LORD's people
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:17 clearly states Jehoiada made a covenant involving the LORD, the king, and the people that they would be God's people, emphasizing the religious restoration and unity.

questions.question: What action did the people take against the house of Baal as described in 2 Kings 11:18?
options: They broke down its altars and images and killed Mattan the priest
They renovated the house and made offerings
They ignored it and continued worshiping Baal secretly
They made a covenant to tolerate Baal worship
questions.correctAnswer: They broke down its altars and images and killed Mattan the priest
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:18 describes that the people thoroughly destroyed Baal's altars and images and slew Mattan the priest, signifying a decisive rejection of idolatry.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 11:19, through which gate did they bring down the king to his house?
questions.correctAnswer: The gate of the guard
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:19 states that they brought down the king by the way of the gate of the guard to the king's house, indicating a formal and guarded procession.

questions.question: How did the people respond after Jehoash was made king according to 2 Kings 11:20?
options: They rejoiced and the city was quiet
They rebelled against the priest's authority
They fled the city in fear
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced and the city was quiet
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:20 notes that all the people rejoiced and the city was in quiet, marking peace and approval after the coup and the death of Athaliah.

questions.question: How old was Jehoash when he began his reign according to 2 Kings 11:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven years old
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:21 explicitly states Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign, indicating a child king protected and led by the priest Jehoiada.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of covenant loyalty between God, king, and people as seen in 2 Kings 11:17?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 12:24
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:24 similarly admonishes the people to serve the LORD faithfully, reflecting the covenant loyalty seen in 2 Kings 11:17 between the LORD, king, and people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the typology of Jehoash's protection and anointing as a foreshadowing of Christ's kingship?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 1:32
questions.explanation: Luke 1:32 foretells Jesus as king over Israel, a foreshadowing typology connected to Jehoash's hidden protection and anointing in 2 Kings 11:12, symbolizing God's preservation of rightful kingship.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in the narrative of Jehoash's reign starting in 2 Kings 11, especially seen in the contrast of Athaliah's reign and the restoration by Jehoiada?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The chapter exhibits chiasm by contrasting the chaos and idolatry under Athaliah with the covenantal restoration and worship under Jehoiada and Jehoash, emphasizing thematic reversal and restoration.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'covenant' (ברית, berith) as used in 2 Kings 11:17?
options: A solemn agreement or treaty between parties
questions.correctAnswer: A solemn agreement or treaty between parties
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'berith' (covenant) in 2 Kings 11:17 refers to a solemn, binding agreement between God, the king, and the people, foundational to Israel's relationship with God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 11:18, Mattan was appointed an officer over the house of the LORD after the destruction of Baal's temple.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:18 states that Mattan, the priest of Baal, was slain before the altars. The priest then appointed officers over the house of the LORD, indicating Mattan was not appointed but killed.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoiada gave the captains of hundreds king David's spears and shields as recorded in 2 Kings 11:10.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 11:10 details that Jehoiada gave king David's spears and shields to the captains, symbolizing the authority and protection for the king's guard.

questions.question: Which passage in the Old Testament shows a similar event to Athaliah's destruction of the royal seed in 2 Kings 11:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 1:15-22
questions.explanation: Exodus 1:15-22 recounts Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew male infants, similar to Athaliah's attempt to destroy the royal seed in 2 Kings 11:1, showing a parallel theme of attempted annihilation of a chosen lineage.

questions.question: What was the role of Jehosheba in preserving the Davidic line according to 2 Kings 11:2-3?
options: She stole Joash from among the slain sons and hid him in the house of the LORD
She led the army against Athaliah
She fled to a foreign land with Joash
questions.correctAnswer: She stole Joash from among the slain sons and hid him in the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 explain Jehosheba saved Joash, hiding him with his nurse in the temple for six years, thus preserving the royal lineage from Athaliah's massacre.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is demonstrated by Jehosheba hiding Joash to preserve the Davidic line despite Athaliah's murderous intent?
options: God’s providential preservation of His covenant promises
The sovereignty of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential preservation of His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Jehosheba’s act in hiding Joash preserves the royal seed, showing God's providence in maintaining His covenant with David despite human evil (2 Kings 11:2). This aligns with God's faithfulness to His promises (Psalm 89:34-37).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly reflected in Jehoiada’s strategic planning and execution to protect the young king and overthrow Athaliah?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom
questions.explanation: Jehoiada’s careful organization of guards and a covenant to protect the king demonstrates God’s wisdom working through His priest to accomplish His righteous purpose (2 Kings 11:4-9).

questions.question: What does the use of King David's spears and shields in the temple during Joash’s coronation symbolize theologically?
options: The continuity of God's covenant through David’s lineage
The importance of military power in leadership
questions.correctAnswer: The continuity of God's covenant through David’s lineage
questions.explanation: The priest gave the captains David’s spears and shields, symbolizing the legitimacy and divine approval of Joash’s kingship as part of the Davidic covenant (2 Kings 11:10).

questions.question: How does Athaliah’s attempt to destroy all royal seed reflect on human sinfulness according to this chapter?
options: It exemplifies the sinful desire for power and rebellion against God’s appointed order
It shows the human capacity for humility and repentance
It illustrates God’s predestination of evil
It demonstrates human inability to act morally
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the sinful desire for power and rebellion against God’s appointed order
questions.explanation: Athaliah’s wholesale murder of royal offspring reveals the depth of human sin in opposing God’s covenant and appointed kingship (2 Kings 11:1).

questions.question: What combined theological insight do verses 5-6 and verse 11 provide about God's protection of His anointed king?
options: God’s providence ensures the security of His anointed through organized human agency and divine protection
God requires constant military conquest to maintain kingship
God’s protection is limited to the temple precincts only
God’s anointed is protected only by supernatural means
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence ensures the security of His anointed through organized human agency and divine protection
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe a strategic guard system, and verse 11 shows the guard protecting the king around the temple, illustrating how God providentially uses human organization to safeguard His anointed (2 Kings 11:5-6, 11).

questions.question: How does the covenant made by Jehoiada between the LORD, the king, and the people in verse 17 reveal the doctrine of sanctification?
options: It shows the corporate commitment to holiness and consecration to God
It indicates that kingship grants automatic sanctity
It suggests that sanctification is only individual
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the corporate commitment to holiness and consecration to God
questions.explanation: The covenant uniting the LORD, king, and people signifies their sanctification as God's holy community, reflecting collective dedication to God's holiness (2 Kings 11:17).

questions.question: What theological significance does the destruction of Baal's house and the killing of Mattan the priest in verse 18 have in the redemptive narrative?
options: It signifies the rejection of idolatry and the restoration of true worship of Yahweh
It shows God's endorsement of violent religious intolerance
It emphasizes political motives over spiritual ones
It marks the end of all pagan religions
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the rejection of idolatry and the restoration of true worship of Yahweh
questions.explanation: The breaking down of Baal’s altars and slaying of his priest indicates God's judgment on idolatry and the re-establishment of covenant worship, pivotal in Israel’s redemptive history (2 Kings 11:18).

questions.question: In what way does Jehoiada’s oath-taking with captains and rulers before revealing the king (verse 4) reflect the theological principle of covenant faithfulness?
options: It illustrates the necessity of solemn covenant to ensure communal loyalty to God’s appointed ruler
It implies that human oaths can override divine commands
It was a political tactic without theological significance
It shows that only priests can govern
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the necessity of solemn covenant to ensure communal loyalty to God’s appointed ruler
questions.explanation: Jehoiada’s oath binds the leaders to God’s covenant purposes, demonstrating the theological gravity of covenant faithfulness to God’s anointed (2 Kings 11:4).

questions.question: How does the public anointing and crowning of Joash in the temple (verse 12) foreshadow Christ’s kingship in biblical theology?
options: It prefigures the messianic king anointed by God to rule righteously
It shows the failure of earthly kings to represent God
It relates only to Old Testament priesthood
It symbolizes the end of kingship
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the messianic king anointed by God to rule righteously
questions.explanation: Joash’s anointing in the temple as king anticipates Christ’s messianic kingship, anointed to reign in righteousness (2 Kings 11:12; Psalm 2:6).

questions.question: What does the violent death of Athaliah outside the temple precincts (verses 15-16) teach about the holiness of God's house and divine justice?
options: That divine justice respects the sanctity of God's house by executing judgment outside it
That God condones violence within His temple
That the temple is a place of refuge for all sinners
questions.correctAnswer: That divine justice respects the sanctity of God's house by executing judgment outside it
questions.explanation: Jehoiada commands Athaliah be killed outside the temple to preserve its holiness, showing reverence for God’s sanctuary even amid administering justice (2 Kings 11:15-16).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal understanding arises from the covenant in verse 17 and the people's destruction of Baal's house in verse 18?
options: The renewal of covenant faithfulness leads to the purging of idolatry and sanctification of the community
The covenant was merely political, unrelated to religious reform
Idolatry is tolerated under the new covenant
Sanctification is only individual without corporate implications
questions.correctAnswer: The renewal of covenant faithfulness leads to the purging of idolatry and sanctification of the community
questions.explanation: The covenant renewal (v.17) results in decisive action against idolatry (v.18), demonstrating sanctification through covenant loyalty and rejection of false worship (2 Kings 11:17-18).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the violent overthrow of Athaliah in 2 Kings 11 contradicts the concept of a loving God. What does 2 Kings 11:13-16 actually teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God’s justice requires righteous judgment even against evil to uphold holiness and covenant order
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice requires righteous judgment even against evil to uphold holiness and covenant order
questions.explanation: The chapter shows that Athaliah’s execution was a just act to remove evil and preserve God’s holy order, reflecting God's justice and holiness (2 Kings 11:13-16; Romans 12:19).

questions.question: What does the rejoicing of all the people upon Joash’s coronation and the city’s resulting quietness (verse 20) reveal about God’s providential rule?
options: God brings peace and stability through His anointed king
Peace is unrelated to divine intervention
Quietness means fear of God’s wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God brings peace and stability through His anointed king
questions.explanation: The people's joy and peace after Joash’s enthronement illustrate God’s providential blessing and the establishment of rightful rule (2 Kings 11:20).

questions.question: How does the age of Jehoash at his ascension (verse 21) emphasize the theme of divine sovereignty over human weakness in this chapter?
options: God can accomplish His purposes even through a child king, showing divine sovereignty over human limitations
Young kings are ineffective and not chosen by God
Age determines spiritual maturity and authority
Divine sovereignty depends on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: God can accomplish His purposes even through a child king, showing divine sovereignty over human limitations
questions.explanation: Jehoash’s youth underscores God’s power to fulfill His plans regardless of human weakness or inexperience (2 Kings 11:21).

questions.question: What combined insight about divine-human cooperation in governance is shown by Jehoiada’s oath (verse 4) and the guards’ faithful obedience (verse 9)?
options: God works through human covenant commitment and faithful obedience to establish righteous rule
Only priests are responsible for governance
questions.correctAnswer: God works through human covenant commitment and faithful obedience to establish righteous rule
questions.explanation: Jehoiada’s covenant and the captains’ obedience show God’s providence using human agents who commit and act faithfully to support His purposes (2 Kings 11:4, 9).
